source_name: NBS – Register podľa PSD2 (register of payment institutions, EMIs, AISP/PISP agents)
why_relevant: Authoritative enumeration of every non-bank payment institution, e-money institution and PSD2 service provider licensed or passported into SK. This is the master actor list from which the whole acquirer/PSP/fintech cell can be snowballed; a machine-readable JSON endpoint (https://subjekty.nbs.sk/api/psd2) was referenced in search results, enabling repeatable structured collection.

source_name: NBS – news/aktuality on opening payment systems to non-bank PSPs
why_relevant: Regulator communications flag structural changes in who may access payment infrastructure — a leading indicator of new acquirers/PSPs entering SK and of soft-POS/instant-payment enablement.

source_name: Worldline Slovensko – merchant services / platobné terminály
why_relevant: Pan-European acquirer/terminal provider with a dedicated SK site and a SK lead-gen microsite (chcemterminal.sk). Product pages reveal terminal models deployed in SK (Yomani, Valina, Axium DX8000) — useful for estimating the installed base composition and refresh cycles.

source_name: SONET / Payten Slovensko (paytenpos.sk)
why_relevant: Terminal technology vendor and softPOS provider (30+ years in CZ/SK), direct competitor/peer in POS estate supply; publishes softPOS positioning and all-in-one ECR+terminal devices relevant to SK e-kasa integration.

source_name: SKPAY, a. s. (formerly SPPS) – payment & e-money institution, POS acceptance
why_relevant: Slovak-owned payment and e-money institution (est. 2012, IČO 46552723) that claims card acceptance for 28,000+ POS terminals in SK, plus Post-office-linked services (Epoukaz, poštová karta) and VIAMO. A rare non-bank acquirer publishing its own estate size and merchant terms.

source_name: VIAMO (mobile P2P / QR payments, SK)
why_relevant: Domestic mobile payment scheme relevant to QR/account-to-account merchant acceptance — an alternative rail competing with card POS. Its FAQ/limits pages and press coverage carry adoption numbers.

source_name: TrustPay, a.s. (Trust Pay) – Bratislava-based PSP / card acquirer
why_relevant: SK-licensed cross-border PSP and card acquiring partner to other gateways (e.g. GoPay). Its partners page maps the SK/CEE gateway-to-acquirer dependency chain; SK-filed accounts under IČO 36865800 give revenue proxies for e-commerce acquiring volume.

source_name: Payout One (payout.one) – NBS-supervised money-movement infrastructure
why_relevant: SK-licensed, NBS-supervised payment infrastructure fintech; publishes its own gateway comparison content for the SK market (a de-facto competitive map of GoPay/Comgate/TrustPay) alongside product/licensing claims.

source_name: Besteron (Pay Solutions a.s. / Solitea) – Slovak payment gateway
why_relevant: Slovak NBS-regulated payment gateway; reported 1,500+ e-shops at the time of Solitea's 2022 majority acquisition. Gives an SK-domestic e-commerce merchant-count datapoint and an ownership/consolidation storyline.

source_name: Comgate (comgate.sk / comgate.cz) – CZ/SK gateway and acquirer
why_relevant: Publishes hard operating metrics (21,000+ merchants, >CZK 53bn annual processed volume as of Jan 2026 per Wikipedia summary) across CZ/SK/PL/HU/RO — one of the few SK-active PSPs disclosing merchant counts and volumes.

source_name: GoPay – payment methods and merchant documentation for the SK market
why_relevant: GoPay's SK knowledge base enumerates every payment method live in SK (bank buttons, wallets, BNPL, card schemes) — an unusually precise, continuously updated map of the SK online payment method landscape. GoPay reports a 7,000+ merchant portfolio and uses TrustPay as card acquirer.

source_name: Register účtovných závierok (registeruz.sk) – statutory financial statements & annual reports
why_relevant: Primary-source filings for every SK-incorporated payment institution, EMI and acquirer subsidiary (mandatory from FY2013). Annual reports of licensed PIs often contain transaction volumes, merchant counts and terminal estates not published anywhere else.

source_name: Obchodný register SR (orsr.sk)
why_relevant: Legal-entity ground truth for SK payment actors: legal form, branch status of foreign acquirers (e.g. Global Payments s.r.o., organizačná zložka), directors, share capital and scope of business (predmet činnosti) — which reveals licensed activities.

source_name: FinReport.sk – SK fintech/banking trade press
why_relevant: Local trade outlet that reports concrete SK payment metrics sourced from PSPs and banks (e.g. a piece on QR payments passing 32,000 transactions / EUR 1m+ volume). Often the only public channel where non-bank actors release SK-specific numbers.

source_name: BOWA – zoznam integrátorov e-kasa (list of e-kasa integrators)
why_relevant: SK-specific: e-kasa (fiscal cash register) integrators are the channel through which POS terminals reach small merchants. This list enumerates software vendors bridging ECR and payment terminals — actors invisible to payment statistics but decisive for terminal penetration.

source_name: Mordor Intelligence – Slovakia POS Terminal Market report
why_relevant: Commercial market-sizing of the SK POS terminal market with vendor shares. Paywalled, but the free summary/TOC reliably names the vendors and segments the analyst considers material — useful as a cross-check on the actor map.

source_name: paymentproviders.io – Slovak payment providers directory
why_relevant: Aggregator claiming 200+ gateway comparisons filtered to the SK market — a fast way to enumerate long-tail PSPs serving SK that never appear in local press. Low credibility on facts, high value as a name-harvesting pointer.

source_name: Visa Slovensko – tlačové centrum (visa.sk press releases)
why_relevant: Visa's Slovak-language press centre publishes country-level payment behaviour findings (contactless share of Visa transactions, e-commerce, travel spend) that no bank or regulator releases in the same framing.

source_name: Visa Slovensko newsroom on Mynewsdesk
why_relevant: Visa's actively used SK distribution channel; carries the CEE Travel & Payment Intentions Study and other survey-based country data with structured dates and full text — easier to harvest than visa.sk.

source_name: Visa Corporate Newsroom / Visa Perspectives (global + CEE)
why_relevant: Parent newsroom carries CEE-level studies and executive quotes (e.g. Visa CEE CEO statements on contactless share in Europe) that contextualise SK numbers and often precede local releases.

source_name: Visa Europe blog – Central Eastern Europe contactless insight posts
why_relevant: Example of scheme-published CEE country breakdowns (contactless share of Visa transactions, contactless-enabled card and POS terminal penetration incl. Slovakia) — the kind of metric only the scheme can produce.

source_name: Mastercard Newsroom – Europe / EEMEA press releases
why_relevant: Mastercard's regional newsroom is the upstream publisher of the SK consumer payment surveys that Slovak media then re-report; also hosts Mastercard Economics Institute trend pieces.

source_name: fontech.startitup.sk – Apple Pay / Google Pay SK bank-support tracker
why_relevant: Maintained overview of which SK banks support which wallet — a de-facto wallet-penetration register that neither Apple nor Google publishes for Slovakia.

source_name: Loomis SK, a.s. – Slovak site (preprava a spracovanie hotovosti)
why_relevant: Largest CIT/cash-processing operator in SK (ex-G4S Cash Solutions SK); service pages reveal cash-cycle capabilities (ATM replenishment, recycling, NBS-licensed authenticity checking) and, via group reporting, cash-volume direction.

source_name: FinStat.sk – company financials for Loomis SK, a.s. (IČO 36394238)
why_relevant: Filed revenue/profit series for the dominant SK CIT operator is a proxy for national cash-handling volume; also confirms the G4S→Loomis name change (2013) needed for entity resolution.

source_name: FinStat.sk – Euronet Services Slovakia, spol. s r.o. (IČO 35854448)
why_relevant: Financials of the main independent (non-bank) ATM deployer entity in SK; revenue trend is a direct read on IAD ATM economics and surcharge-driven withdrawal volumes.

source_name: Euronet ATM Solutions – operator/product site (EU outsourcing & CIT ATMs)
why_relevant: Euronet's IAD/outsourcing arm describes ATM-as-a-service, CIT-ATM and branch-outsourcing offers sold into CEE incl. SK; useful for actor mapping and competitive positioning of independent deployers.

source_name: eBankomaty.sk – SK ATM directory
why_relevant: Third-party directory of ATMs in Slovakia by operator/bank; usable as an independent estimate of ATM fleet size and operator mix, including non-bank deployers.

source_name: OMA.sk – bankomat POI dataset (OpenStreetMap-derived)
why_relevant: Open geospatial inventory of ATM points in SK with operator tags; the only easily licensable machine-readable ATM location layer for footprint/density analysis.
